summary: Jayashree D. Sathe works in Indology and linguistics. At Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, she served as editor-in-chief (attested 2011) and later as Professor-Editor for the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).

Jaś Elsner is a historian and archaeologist. He studied at Cambridge (BA, PhD), Courtauld Institute, and Harvard. His posts include positions at Jesus College, Courtauld Institute, Corpus Christi College, and Professor of Late Antique Art at Oxford (2014).

Jean Boisselier was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École des Beaux-Arts, École du Louvre, and the Sorbonne under Philippe Stern and Pierre Dupont. He served at EFEO, National Museum of Cambodia, and Sorbonne Nouvelle.

Jean Buhot (1885–1952) specialized in archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He was appointed Professor of Chinese and Japanese Art at the École du Louvre in 1936 and Professor of Japanese at INALCO in 1940.

Jean Carl (1900–1941) was a researcher in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1928–1937) and the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan (~1937–1941).

Jean Dantinne is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Liège and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He held posts as lecturer in Chinese at the University of Liège (1975) and professor at Université catholique de Louvain (1983).

Jean Deloche (1929–2019) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as director of the Alliance Française of Madras (1962–1966), researcher and associate member at EFEO, and associate member at the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1966–2019).

Jean Deny (1879–1963) was a linguist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, where he later taught (~1908–1949), and subsequently held a post at Georgetown University (1949–1953).

Jean Ferdinand Caius (1877–1944) worked in Indology and related fields. He studied at St. Mary's College, St Beuno's, and the University of Paris, later serving at the Haffkine Institute (1924–1932) and St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1932).

Jean Filliozat (1906–1982) was an Indologist who studied at EPHE and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Renou. He held professorships at EPHE and Collège de France, and directed EFEO and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Haudry (1934–2023) was a linguist and Indologist. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure and Sorbonne Nouvelle under Armand Minard, he held academic appointments at Jean Moulin University - Lyon 3 (~1973–2002) and EPHE (~1990–2002).

Jean Herbert (1897–1980) worked in religious studies and Indology, having studied under Sri Aurobindo in 1934. He served at the League of Nations and the United Nations, and taught Eastern mythologies at the University of Geneva (1954–1964).

Jean Kellens is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He studied at the University of Liège and under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg, holding posts at Mainz (~1974–1993) and the Collège de France (from 1993).

Jean Petitot is a philosopher and linguist. An alumnus of École Polytechnique (~1964–1967), he held posts at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~1983) and served as director at École Polytechnique (~1992–2006).

Jean Philippe Vogel (1871–1958) was an Indologist and archaeologist. Educated at the University of Amsterdam under C. C. Uhlenbeck and Kern, he served with the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and was director at Leiden University.

Jean Przyluski (1885–1944) studied Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics at EPHE and ENFOM under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at EFEO, INALCO, EPHE (1926–1944), and the Collège de France (1930–1944).

Jean Varenne (1926–1997) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD at EPHE under Jean Haudry. He taught Sanskrit at Aix-Marseille University (1962–1980) and Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (1981–1987).

Jean-Antoine Dubois (1765–1848) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at the Séminaire des Missions Étrangères de Paris. He directed the Seminary of Pondicherry (1813–1819) and became supérieur of the Paris Foreign Missions Society in 1836.

Jean-Baptiste Biot (1774–1862) studied at École Polytechnique under Gaspard Monge and Pierre-Simon Laplace. His career spanned mathematics, astronomy, and physics, with professorships at École Centrale de Beauvais, Collège de France (1800–1862), and the University of Paris.

Jean-Denis Lanjuinais (1753–1827) worked in Indology and religious studies. After earning a doctorate of laws from the University of Rennes (~1768–1771), he served there as Professor of Canonic Law (1775) and joined the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (1808).
